title: Calcutta High Court Orders Arrest of Delhi Capitals Cricketer Abishek Porel Over Rape Allegations
excerpt: The court directed police to apprehend the 23-year-old Bengal batsman and seize his electronic devices after a woman accused him of sexual assault under a false promise of marriage.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Calcutta High Court ordered arrest of cricketer Abishek Porel over rape allegations on July 14.
  • A woman accused Porel of sexual assault under a false promise of marriage over three years.
  • The court directed seizure of Porel's electronic devices to prevent dissemination of intimate photos.
  • Porel, 23, denies the allegations; next hearing scheduled for August 11.
  • The Calcutta High Court ordered police on July 14 to apprehend Delhi Capitals cricketer Abishek Porel over rape and criminal assault charges
  • A woman filed a complaint at Mogra Police Station alleging Porel had a sexual relationship with her under a false promise of marriage over three years
  • The court also directed seizure of Porel's electronic devices to prevent dissemination of intimate photographs of the complainant
  • Porel, 23, has denied the allegations; the next hearing is scheduled for August 11

The Calcutta High Court has directed police to urgently trace and apprehend Delhi Capitals and Bengal cricketer Abishek Porel after a woman accused him of rape under a false promise of marriage. Justice Saugata Bhattacharyya, in an order passed on July 14, noted that Porel and one other accused remain at large despite police efforts to arrest them.

The court also ordered the seizure of Porel's electronic devices, stating that "obnoxious data stored therein shall not be further disseminated" — a reference to the complainant's allegation that the cricketer recorded intimate moments without consent.

"She claims the cricketer engaged in a physical relationship under the repeated promise of marriage but began distancing himself over the past year."

The Allegations

A case was registered against Porel at Mogra Police Station in West Bengal's Hooghly district under multiple sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and the Information Technology Act. The charges include rape, criminal assault, and criminal intimidation — all non-bailable offenses.

According to the complaint filed by the woman and her mother, the complainant alleges she was in a relationship with Porel for approximately three years. She claims the cricketer engaged in a physical relationship under the repeated promise of marriage but began distancing himself over the past year. The complaint also accuses him of physical and mental abuse, including violent sexual acts against her will.

Porel has strongly denied all allegations. In earlier statements to media, he attributed the complaint to his rising cricket profile. "I am playing well now, so various things are coming up," he was quoted as saying, adding that he would respond in detail after the police complete their inquiry.

A left-handed top-order batsman, Porel has represented Delhi Capitals in the Indian Premier League since 2023. He scored 108 runs across four innings for the franchise in the most recently concluded IPL season and has traveled with the India A team to the UK and Australia.

A Troubling Pattern

Emerging Pattern in Cricket Allegations
›Similar allegations against players like Vipraj Nigam and Yash Dayal
›Raising questions about accountability in sports

The case adds to a string of similar allegations against emerging Indian cricketers in recent months. Players including Vipraj Nigam and Yash Dayal have also faced police investigations for comparable offenses, raising questions about accountability and conduct among young professional athletes.

The court has asked police to file a compliance report by August 14. The next hearing in the matter is set for August 11.
